ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the upper left end is the positive input terminal. After passing through a resistor labeled R with resistance 200 Ω, it reaches the middle node; this middle node is connected downward to a Zener diode labeled VZ, and the lower end of the diode is connected to the bottom common negative terminal/lower rail. The middle node also passes rightward through a resistor labeled RL with resistance 500 Ω and is connected to the right-side positive output terminal. The right-side negative output terminal is on the bottom lower rail, and the output voltage is labeled Uo. Reasoning: The problem states that the output terminal is open-circuited, so no load current flows out of the output terminal; the current in the right-side 500 Ω resistor RL is 0, so the voltage drop across RL is 0, and the potential of the positive output terminal is equal to the potential of the middle node. The Zener diode VZ is connected between the middle node and the lower rail, and the given regulated voltage is UZ = 10 V, so the middle node is clamped at 10 V relative to the lower rail. Therefore, the open-circuit output voltage UO = 10 V.

raw_record.question_text: In the circuit shown above, the input voltage is 12 V, the output end is open-circuited, and the Zener diode \(V_Z\) has a stable voltage \(U_Z = 10\) V. Then the open-circuit output voltage \(U_O\) is ________ V.

method.method_draft: First describe the image topology. Since the output end is open, no current flows out of the output terminal, so no current flows through the 500 Ω resistor RL. Therefore the output positive terminal has the same voltage as the central node. The Zener diode is connected between that node and the lower rail and is specified as stabilizing at UZ = 10 V, so the central node is clamped to 10 V relative to the lower rail. Hence UO = 10 V.
